page_placements.theme: Feature-specific error correction and anisotropic perturbation responses

record.tranche_reason: The post reports experiments on channel-amplification maxima and feature-like directions, but does not test superposition, capacity competition, polysemantic neurons, SAE recovery or completeness, or whether superposed features are one-dimensional.
record.gate_note: The post measures error-correction scores and geometry for candidate directions it calls ur-features. Those measurements do not test any listed version of the superposition or polysemanticity claim. The author explicitly distinguishes these maxima from conventional SAE features. The post also reports no result that tests how features are stored when their number exceeds the available dimensions.
record.test_reason: The post defines a channel-amplification (denoising) score and reports its maxima in GPT-2 and Llama MLP layers. It does not measure whether features are stored in superposition, whether polysemanticity comes from capacity competition, how much SAEs recover, or whether features are one-dimensional. It mentions superposition and SAE naturality only as background and argument. The record's T6/discusses is correct.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author also guesses that most amp maxima do not behave like conventional features, except perhaps the abstract-noun one. He suggests they reflect computational functions, and flags 'just PCA with bells and whistles' as the likeliest deflationary explanation.
record.recipe_differences: The post defines and optimizes a channel-amplification score to find denoising directions; it does not apply the Toy Models of Superposition method or test its feature-storage predictions.
record.method_sensitivity: The maxima depend on training protocol, spherical whitening, threshold choice, data distribution, and gradient-ascent setup; the post says changing the data to bigram statistics alters some maxima.

fits_no_version.finding: Amp-score maxima form a small set (3–6) of attractor directions in GPT-2 and Llama MLP layers. They depend on setup, whitening, threshold and data, and have specific pairwise geometry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP layers have a small number of directions they most strongly denoise or amplify. These are findable by gradient ascent on a channel-amplification score and are partly a function of the weights.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features score higher than test activations, and coarse parents score higher than children (0.140 vs 0.104). The author states SAE features are not even approximately local amp maxima.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionary features are partially, but not maximally, denoised by the model's MLP computation.

record.problems: The principal experiments concern one small, unfinetuned model and a particular MLP layer; the author notes data and setup dependence. The post does not provide uncertainty estimates for the reported measurements, and says the candidate directions may not behave like conventional features.
record.rows_left_out: Commenter David Africa's separate experiments were not entered as rows because they are reported by a commenter rather than as the post author's experiments.

untested.parts: All: no toy model, no sparsity sweep, no measure of feature-storage geometry.
All: no measure of capacity competition or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
All: polysemantic neurons are not studied.
All: no measure of features spread across neurons or of SAE recovery.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features are not measured. The author only argues that SAEs may reflect the data rather than the model's computation.
All: the dimensionality of superposed features is not tested. The low-dimensional atlas (r9) concerns the span of the maxima, not feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The commenter's replication (David Africa) is correctly excluded as a non-author result. The gpt2-XL non-convex basin appendix is unrowed but bears on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse overcomplete features are stored as overlapping near-orthogonal directions, and whether sparsity produces a transition or regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition, including whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure, or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Whether real models spread features across neurons or whether an SAE recovers sparse model features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of the model's representation.
Whether the features involved in superposition are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.
